lines.text: In sixteen fifty six, two South Indian kingdoms fought a war that people remembered, not for its battles, but for noses.

lines.text: On one side was Tirumala Nayak, king of Madurai. On the other, Kanthirava Narasaraja, ruler of Mysore.

lines.text: Madurai had sided with Mysore's enemy, the Sultan of Bijapur. When the Bijapur army went home, Mysore struck back.

lines.text: Its army marched south under a general named Hampaiya.

lines.text: Old accounts say his soldiers cut off the noses of the people they captured, even ordinary villagers.

lines.text: Why noses? Historians have read it as punishment, as humiliation, perhaps even as a ritual.
Tirumala Nayak was old and ill. He called on an ally, Raghunatha Sethupathi, ruler of Ramnad.

lines.text: Then Madurai struck back. Its army marched into Mysore country, and accounts say it hunted noses too.

lines.text: Tirumala Nayak died soon after, around sixteen fifty nine.
